title: The Weekend Home Reset: Storage and Cleaning Supplies
excerpt: Clear bins, latching boxes and the cleaning staples that make a one-weekend declutter actually stick.

body.p: Decluttering fails when stuff has nowhere to go. Here's a simple two-day plan: sort and bin on Saturday, then deep-clean the newly empty surfaces on Sunday.

Pull everything out of one area, like the garage, a closet or under the bed, and sort it into keep, donate and toss. Keepers go into bins you can see into, labeled on the short end so the label shows when they're stacked.
For closets and under-bed space, the smaller latching clip boxes are easier to lift and keep out dust.
Once shelves and floors are clear, it's the easiest time to clean them. Work top to bottom: wipe high surfaces first, then counters, then floors.

ul: One in, one out: when something new comes home, something old leaves.
Keep a donate bin by the door and drop it off when it's full.
Put wipes in every bathroom and the kitchen so quick cleanups actually happen.
